tasks.short: Arrange consultations, prepare the case summary, consult other professionals and agencies on therapies and resources, and note the advice.

steps.what: Psychologist arranges consultations with other professionals by e-mail
Psychologist prepares the case summary for consultation
Psychologist consults with other professionals, agencies or universities to discuss therapies and treatments
Psychologist notes the advice in the record

tasks.design: Recurring multidisciplinary consultation slots sit in the shared agenda ({CALENDAR}) and cases are entered on a short request form, so consultations are not arranged by e-mail. The case summary template fills scores, goals and treatment so far from the record ({OTHER}), anonymised where the client has not consented to sharing. Advice is noted in a structured field. Consulting stays with the psychologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Consultations were arranged by e-mail and summaries written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared agendas and record templates fill summaries from existing data.
tasks.still_hard: Outside agencies use their own systems.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from a colleague the technique that unlocks a stuck case.

evidence.claim: Record templates can fill case summaries from scores and goals already recorded.
Session notes and test results are health data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the consultation need to advice noted; changing treatment is outside.
Input contract: client consent for sharing; fallback is an anonymised summary.

incremental.description: Psychologist anonymises summaries where consent is missing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few consultations; high: many cases discussed each month.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop training programs and materials, teach and supervise staff and students, schedule sessions, and record supervision hours and assessments.

steps.what: Psychologist develops training programs and materials for staff and students
Psychologist schedules training sessions and supervision by e-mail
Psychologist directs and participates in training and supervises trainees
Psychologist records supervision hours and assessments in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Training modules and anonymised teaching cases sit in a shared library ({DOCS}) that the psychologist adapts instead of building each program. Sessions and supervision run as series in the learning system ({LMS}), which also holds each trainee's portfolio of supervision hours and assessments, replacing the spreadsheet. Teaching and supervising stay with the psychologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programs were built from scratch and supervision hours kept in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems hold schedules and trainee portfolios.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching cases must be fully anonymised.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a trainee reflect on a session that went wrong.

reach.learn: Whether supervision hours are up to date.

evidence.claim: Learning systems can hold schedules and trainee portfolios with hours and assessments.

assumptions: Boundary: from the training need to hours recorded; formal registration of trainees is outside.
Input contract: library kept by the training team; fallback is building from scratch.
Teaching and supervision do not change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off sessions; high: many trainees with portfolios.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review guidelines and research, design the program with psychiatrists and staff, write the program and protocols, check them against accreditation criteria, check the program with the team, and submit it for accreditation.

steps.what: Psychologist screens guidelines and research for the program

loop.input: Records from a literature search and the psychologist's include or exclude labels so far.
loop.output: The records reordered so the most likely relevant come first.
loop.check: The psychologist labels every record shown; a stop rule fixed beforehand is tested on known relevant studies.
loop.stop: Stops when the fixed run of irrelevant records is reached and all known relevant studies were found.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword filters miss studies or return thousands of records.

steps.what: Psychologist plans and develops the psychological service program with psychiatrists and staff
Psychologist writes the program description and protocols
Psychologist checks the program against accreditation criteria
Psychologist checks the final program with the team
Psychologist submits the accredited program for accreditation on the accrediting body's portal

tasks.design: Literature screening uses active learning: records are reordered while the psychologist labels them, with a stop rule fixed beforehand. The program template has a section per accreditation criterion, and a checklist shows which criteria are not yet covered, instead of checking by hand. Designing the program with psychiatrists and staff stays with the psychologist, who submits it personally once the team has checked it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records were screened one by one and criteria checked by hand at the end.
tasks.enabler_now: Active learning screening tools; templates mapped to accreditation criteria.
tasks.human_edge: Getting psychiatrists and nurses to agree on one program.
tasks.altitude: The psychologist labels and designs instead of screening and checking.

reach.learn: Whether the program is accredited first time.

evidence.claim: ASReview puts likely relevant records first while a person screens.
In simulations on six review datasets, active learning needed 63.9% to 91.7% fewer records screened to find 95% of relevant ones.

assumptions: Boundary: from the program need to the program submitted; running the program is outside.
Input contract: accreditation criteria published; fallback is checking by hand.
The psychologist labels every included record.
Team members' time does not change.
research_questions: Is the program accredited at first submission?

incremental.description: Psychologist updates the criteria checklist after changes.

approvals.approved_version: The program as checked with the team in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small updates; high: new programs with broad literature.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange talks with schools, agencies and businesses, prepare materials, give educational, outreach and prevention talks, and collect feedback.

steps.what: Psychologist arranges talks with schools and agencies by e-mail
Psychologist prepares talk materials for the audience
Psychologist provides educational programs, outreach programs or prevention talks
Psychologist collects and tallies paper feedback forms

tasks.design: Schools and agencies request talks on a booking form on the practice website with topic, audience and date options, so arrangements are not made by e-mail. Talks come from a library of slide sets per topic and audience ({DOCS}) that the psychologist adapts. Feedback is collected on a short online form shown at the end, and scores are tallied automatically. Giving the talks stays with the psychologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Talks were arranged by e-mail, materials remade and feedback tallied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking forms, slide libraries and online feedback forms are easy to run.
tasks.still_hard: Each audience needs its own examples.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a class of teenagers to talk about stress.

reach.learn: Whether talks are booked earlier in the year.

evidence.claim: Booking forms, slide libraries and online feedback forms are easy to run.

assumptions: Boundary: from the talk request to feedback tallied; invoicing is outside.
Input contract: library kept by the psychologist; fallback is e-mail and paper.
Schools fill the booking form in about the time an e-mail took.
Audiences fill the online form in about the time paper took.
research_questions: Do feedback scores rise as talks are refined?

incremental.description: Psychologist keeps the slide library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few, very different talks; high: many talks on the same topics.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The psychologist keeps consulting, teaching, designing programs and giving talks; e-mail arranging, record screening and spreadsheets shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A psychologist with more time for prevention.
